events.title: Movie Magic: Greatest Film Themes for Violin & Piano
events.time: 2:00 PM · Manitou Opera House, 325 Main Street, Manitou, MB
events.description: Experience the music behind some of cinema's greatest moments — live at the Manitou Opera House! The magic of the movies is coming to the Manitou Opera House! Join Winnipeg-based violinist Amir Bissen and pianist Fan-En Chiang for an intimate live concert featuring some of the most unforgettable music from the world of film. From the suspense of Jaws and the adventure of Jurassic Park to the romance of The Godfather, the excitement of James Bond and Star Wars, and the magic of Harry Potter, Movie Magic brings beloved film themes to life in specially curated arrangements for violin and piano. Rather than simply recreating the original orchestral scores, Bissen and Chiang bring their own expressive interpretations to these familiar melodies. Their intimate arrangements offer audiences a fresh and captivating way to experience music that has become woven into popular culture. Whether you're a longtime classical music enthusiast, a devoted movie fan, or simply looking for an entertaining afternoon of live music, Movie Magic promises an experience for audiences of all ages. Sunday, October 4, 2026 2:00 PM Doors open at 1:00 PM Manitou Opera House — Manitou, Manitoba What You'll Hear Travel through some of Hollywood's most memorable musical moments, featuring themes from iconic films and franchises including: Jaws Jurassic Park The Godfather James Bond Star Wars Harry Potter …and more! Hear these familiar themes in a completely new way as they're transformed for violin and piano and performed live in the intimate setting of the historic Manitou Opera House. Meet the Performers Amir Bissen — Violin Winnipeg-based violinist Amir Bissen brings extensive international performing experience to the stage. Bissen began his musical career at an early age, studying at the Purcell School of Music and Royal College of Music in England. His performing career has taken him throughout Europe and includes a Royal Festival Hall debut with the Philharmonia Orchestra. He has also pursued advanced studies with renowned violin pedagogue Zakhar Bron, bringing a wealth of musical experience and artistry to his performances. Fan-En Chiang — Piano Fan-En Chiang is an award-winning Taiwanese-Canadian pianist and composer based in Winnipeg. His performances have included appearances with the Winnipeg Symphony Orchestra, and his musical interests extend beyond the classical repertoire to include film music and video-game soundtracks. Together, Bissen and Chiang are developing themed recital programs that bring familiar and much-loved music to audiences while showcasing the artistry, energy and intimacy of live classical performance. Experience Movie Music Like Never Before You've heard these melodies in movie theatres. Now hear them live, up close and reimagined for violin and piano. Come relive the suspense, adventure, romance and magic of some of cinema's greatest stories through the music that helped make them unforgettable. Movie Magic: Greatest Film Themes for Violin & Piano is an afternoon for movie lovers, music lovers and anyone who enjoys a great live performance.

events.title: Webinar: Fostering Community, Collaboration, and Coexistence in the Sturgeon River Plains Bison Herd’s Stewardship
events.time: 12:00 PM · Watch from anywhere!
events.description: October Native Prairie Speaker Series Webinar Fostering Community, Collaboration, and Coexistence in the Sturgeon River Plains Bison Herd’s Stewardship Tuesday October 6th, 2026 at 12:00pm MT Speaker: Mia Nemeth, Environmental Anthropology graduate student, University of Saskatchewan Register Free: https://shorturl.at/OF2Bu or for government computers: https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_hQj55kYMQACv5WoxxWqqnQ This presentation is FREE! Tune in from anywhere! Everyone welcome! More Information: SK PCAP at 306.352.0472 or pcap@sasktel.net About this Webinar: Saskatchewan was once home to multitudes of plains bison, roaming wild and free across this prairie province’s native grasslands. But did you know that a wild herd of plains bison still calls this province home? One of only two wild, unfenced and free-roaming plains bison herds within this species’ original Canadian range, the Sturgeon River plains bison herd (SRPBH) inhabits the sedge meadows and fescue grasslands of southwestern Prince Albert National Park (PANP). The SRPBH plays an important ecological and cultural role in this landscape and is valued by many individuals and groups, with particular significance for local First Nations and Métis communities. However, the herd is also the source of ongoing conflict. Privately owned agricultural landscapes border the southwestern boundary of PANP – a tempting buffet for an unfenced herd of wild plains bison. The SRPBH seasonally forages in these park-adjacent lands, creating jurisdictional governance complexities and impacting local livelihoods; conflict persists despite official (and unofficial) mitigation efforts. Beyond the social and cultural implications of this herd’s presence, there are concerns over the SRPBH’s future viability since their population has declined by 50%. In this talk Mia Nemeth will discuss how (under the supervision of Dr. Clinton Westman) she gained insight into the diverse perspectives, interests, and concerns influencing the SRPBH’s stewardship. By overviewing her numerous land-based encounters, in-depth interviews, informal conversations, and the quantitative survey used, she aims to emphasize local perspectives and community insights and highlight how this research can help ensure that future collaborative stewardship is effective, representative, and reconciliation minded. About the Speaker: Mia Nemeth is an Environmental Anthropology graduate student at the University of Saskatchewan. She focused her undergraduate studies on environmental anthropology and multispecies issues, driven by a deep connection to, and curiosity for, wildlife and the environments they call home. Throughout her academic journey, and experiences working in applied conservation and nature interpretation, she became increasingly interested in how social and cultural factors shape people’s relationships to the natural world, and how these perspectives influence environmental stewardship. She feels fortunate to be able to apply her experiences and passion for wildlife conservation to her master’s research in her home province of Saskatchewan. She lives in Saskatoon with her partner Éric and their cat Krickett (who chirps like a cricket). Watch from anywhere! Watch from anywhere!

events.title: Agatha's Almanac - Movie Showing
events.time: 7:00 PM · Mennonite Heritage Village, 231 PTH 12N, Steinbach, MB
events.description: MHV Auxiliary presents Agatha’s Almanac Doors open 6:30 pm, coffee and refreshments served Join the MHV Auxiliary for the showing of Agatha’s Almanac, the incredible true story of 90-year-old Agatha Bock. Proceeds from the event go to the MHV Auxiliary, which supports the mission of Mennonite Heritage Village. Synopsis from Agatha’s Almanac 90-year-old Agatha forges a solitary existence on her ancestral farm, preseving heirloom seeds in her handmade universe. Without a drivers license, cell phone, running water, or even a functioning landline Agatha’s daily rituals form a vivid counterpoint to modern life. Shot by an all-female crew, the project captures the handmade materiality inherent in both the medium of film and Agatha’s tactile world. It serves as a powerful conduit for often-overlooked stories, amplifying voices and rural perspectives. Agatha’s life offers a window into the experiences of a nearly lost generation, whose value and ways of living are at risk of fading as the world rapidly changes. Tickets can be purchased online, by phone, or at the front desk.

events.title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
events.time: 7:30 PM · Kenmor Theatre, 130 7TH STREET, Morden, MB
events.description: In Tennessee Williams’ Pulitzer Prize-winning Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, the dysfunctional but wealthy Pollitt family gathers to celebrate aging patriarch Big Daddy’s birthday. But there is more to this gathering than a family reunion– Big Daddy is dying of cancer, and he hasn’t decided which of his sons will inherit the estate. His options include favorite son Brick, who drinks himself into oblivion in order to bear the oppressive expectations of his determined wife, Maggie, or his less-favored son Gooper, his fertile wife Mae, and their five “no-neck monster” children. While sensuous Maggie “the cat” tries to work her wiles to secure a future for them, Brick spirals deeper into despair, crippled by both physical pain and emotional loss. Lurking under every practiced interaction between the Pollitts is an ulterior motive, under every smile, a challenge, and under every statement, the specter of mendacity. For the Pollitts, the truth is as hazy as the late summer sun in Mississippi, and sometimes the only way to find it is to journey through the lies. The production staged by Candlewick Players is a strong drama with mature content the characters must face as they work through the lies in their family... as a result, the play is recommended for an more mature audience.

events.title: Rosemary Siemens - Bring Back the Hymns - Live In Concert!
events.time: 7:00 PM · PW Enns Concert Hall, 783 Mountain Ave, Winkler, Manitoba
events.description: Three generations. One stage. The hymns you grew up singing, in Winkler for one night only. BRING BACK THE HYMNS comes to the PW Enns Concert Hall on Saturday, October 17. Harvest Christian Fellowship presents a benefit concert with international violin sensation Rosemary Siemens and her family. Rosemary has performed four times at New York's Carnegie Hall and was the first violinist ever to perform in the Sistine Chapel at the Vatican since its inception in 1483. She has played in over 25 countries and 40 U.S. states, for two U.S. Presidents and Canadian Prime Ministers, and won Country Gospel Album of the Year at Canada's Gospel Music Awards. Today she leads a global movement to Bring Back the Hymns through the #1 hymn channel on YouTube, with more than 700,000 subscribers and over 200 million views in every corner of the world. This concert is that movement live and in person. Rosemary is joined by her husband, JUNO-nominated saxophonist Eli Bennett, together as the acclaimed duo SaxAndViolin, along with their young sons and Rosemary's parents. Grandparents, parents and grandchildren on one stage, playing the hymns that have been handed down through their family for generations. Expect an evening that travels from Carnegie Hall to the Vatican, from the Colosseum to the Grand Ole Opry and back home to a Manitoba church pew. Timeless hymns, inspirational classics, and the stories behind them, including how gospel music shaped Rosemary's life and continues to touch people around the world. Bring your family. Bring the people who first taught you these hymns. This is a night to sing them out loud together again. Seating is limited and this one will fill up. Get your tickets early. CONCERT DETAILS Saturday, October 17, 2026 PW Enns Concert Hall 783 Mountain Ave, Winkler, MB 7:00 PM Tickets: $40 (donations gratefully accepted) In support of Harvest Christian Fellowship For more info: 1-204-829-3069

events.title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
events.time: 7:30 PM · Kenmor Theatre, 130 7TH STREET, Morden, MB
events.description: In Tennessee Williams’ Pulitzer Prize-winning Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, the dysfunctional but wealthy Pollitt family gathers to celebrate aging patriarch Big Daddy’s birthday. But there is more to this gathering than a family reunion– Big Daddy is dying of cancer, and he hasn’t decided which of his sons will inherit the estate. His options include favorite son Brick, who drinks himself into oblivion in order to bear the oppressive expectations of his determined wife, Maggie, or his less-favored son Gooper, his fertile wife Mae, and their five “no-neck monster” children. While sensuous Maggie “the cat” tries to work her wiles to secure a future for them, Brick spirals deeper into despair, crippled by both physical pain and emotional loss. Lurking under every practiced interaction between the Pollitts is an ulterior motive, under every smile, a challenge, and under every statement, the specter of mendacity. For the Pollitts, the truth is as hazy as the late summer sun in Mississippi, and sometimes the only way to find it is to journey through the lies. The production staged by Candlewick Players is a strong drama with mature content the characters must face as they work through the lies in their family... as a result, the play is recommended for an more mature audience.

events.title: Home Routes Concerts at WAC: Dan McKinnon
events.time: 7:00 PM · Winkler Arts and Culture, 547 Park St,, Winkler, Manitoba
events.description: With a rich baritone voice and a love of storytelling, Dan McKinnon brings the musical traditions and stories of Atlantic Canada to our gallery. Growing up in Halifax, Dan was surrounded by family stories and music, eventually discovering the guitar and the music of Stan Rogers, an influence that helped shape his own approach to songwriting. Over more than 30 years of performing, Dan has taken his songs from coffeehouses and the Halifax Farmers’ Market to audiences across Canada and around the world. Buy your tickets for this concert, as well as others in the series at www.winklerarts.com/2026-27-concert-series/
